announcements.text: session_notify's 'now' mode is RETIRED and passing it FAILS the delivery outright - it is not merely discouraged. 'turn-end' is the default and wakes an idle target immediately, so it loses nothing 'now' ever delivered; 'quiet' is retained for batch notices whose ack contract is the ledger. 'interrupt' is the URGENT tier (#393): it delivers at the SAME boundary as turn-end and adds precedence framing so the target yields its current plan and answers in that turn - never deferred, never a default, spell it explicitly. It is NOT pre-emption: no boundary exists inside a running tool call, so a mid-turn target still queues for its next tool-loop boundary. Legacy interrupt:true UPGRADES a non-quiet resolution to that tier. A 'no wake observed' confirm verdict does NOT mean the target is mid-turn — a mid-turn target returns `queued_pending_drain`. The unconfirmed verdict means the probe read the target idle and no wake was seen inside the 10s cap, so it cannot distinguish 'queued, will drain' from 'folded into a turn-settle window and never re-armed' (fork leshchenko1979/opencrabs#770 — migrated 2026-10-10 from upstream #2003, which was closed NOT_PLANNED with a pointer and NOT fixed: in the settle window the probe reads idle while the turn is still finishing, the notice joins the settling turn, and no wake is re-armed — measured 5m41s undrained). Never re-send on the verdict alone: re-check the target's own store first.

Never grep it with a context flag (-A/-B), and never print a parsed form of it - json.dumps of a single endpoint dict renders the key field verbatim. Read the KEY NAMES only; to compare a value, hash it in place. The read discipline is necessary but not sufficient: the PRINT is the second chokepoint, and it is the one that fails when the read felt safe. A third chokepoint is any TOOL whose output path renders the file's content: a diff, a checksum-and-dump, or a guard that prints a drift diff between two key-bearing copies discloses both. Read the output path before you ship the tool, not after.

announcements.text: infra_mac-cdp-tunnel (endpoint_id 15) was RED for 20 h 18 min: Gatus's own event table reads UNHEALTHY 2026-10-23T10:05:09Z -> HEALTHY 2026-10-24T06:23:09Z, and every probe in that window failed. An earlier version of this entry read '110 results / 0 failures', true only of the window it was read in, four hours before the outage began. THE MECHANISM, read from the endpoint's own definition rather than inferred: it is NOT a Mac-localhost check. The URL is ssh://78.17.187.4:15259 — which `getent hosts` resolves to THIS host, agents — and the body then runs `curl -s --max-time 3 http://localhost:9222/json/version | grep -c Macintosh` ON AGENTS. `grep -c` exits 1 on zero matches, so the probe is red whenever nothing listens on agents' loopback:9222; the probed object is the FORWARDER, not the Mac. THE MAC WAS HEALTHY THROUGHOUT: with the endpoint red, `ssh mac` succeeded and CDP answered Chrome/150.0.7871.1016 with a Macintosh User-Agent. THE DEFECT WAS SUPERVISION, NOW CLOSED AND PROVEN ACROSS A REBOOT. The forwarder was hand-launched every time, so it died and nothing brought it back. announcements.text: session_notify's 'now' mode is RETIRED and passing it FAILS the delivery outright - it is not merely discouraged. 'turn-end' is the default and wakes an idle target immediately, so it loses nothing 'now' ever delivered; 'quiet' is retained for batch notices whose ack contract is the ledger. 'interrupt' is the URGENT tier (#393): it delivers at the SAME boundary as turn-end and adds precedence framing so the target yields its current plan and answers in that turn - never deferred, never a default, spell it explicitly. It is NOT pre-emption: no boundary exists inside a running tool call, so a mid-turn target still queues for its next tool-loop boundary. Legacy interrupt:true UPGRADES a non-quiet resolution to that tier. A 'no wake observed' confirm verdict does NOT mean the target is mid-turn — a mid-turn target returns `queued_pending_drain`. The unconfirmed verdict means the probe read the target idle and no wake was seen inside the 10s cap, so it cannot distinguish 'queued, will drain' from 'folded into a turn-settle window and never re-armed' (fork leshchenko1979/opencrabs#770 — migrated 2026-10-10 from upstream #2003, which was closed NOT_PLANNED with a pointer and NOT fixed: in the settle window the probe reads idle while the turn is still finishing, the notice joins the settling turn, and no wake is re-armed — measured 5m41s undrained). Never re-send on the verdict alone: re-check the target's own store first.
